claims.text: Spiking neural networks with Spike Response Model realize piecewise linear mappings
SNNs can realize both continuous and discontinuous functions, unlike ReLU networks
Provide complexity bounds on SNN size to emulate multi-layer ReLU networks
Establish complexity bounds in reverse direction for one-layer SNNs in continuous setting
The firing mapping of an LSNN (Linear SNN) is piecewise linear (Theorem 9)
For LSNN with only positive weights, the firing time function is increasing and concave (Proposition 10)
SNNs use temporal coding where precise timing of spikes matters

gaps.description: Theoretical analysis limited to linear response function SNNs
No empirical validation of theoretical bounds
Temporal coding focus - rate coding not analyzed
Complexity bounds may not be tight

non_extractable_items.reason: Purely theoretical paper - no experimental validation

summary.main_contribution: Formal theoretical analysis of SNN expressivity compared to ReLU networks
summary.key_finding: SNNs can express both continuous and discontinuous functions with quantifiable complexity bounds
summary.domain: Theoretical machine learning / Neural network expressivity
summary.methodology: Mathematical proofs using Spike Response Model
summary.limitations: Purely theoretical, limited to linear response functions
